children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 7 years old. I'm interested in finding out if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me ask you a few questions to assess your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK at the moment. Does that affect whether I can claim Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, where you live can affect your eligibility for Child Benefit. Let me ask you some follow-up questions to understand your situation better.

**Which country do you currently live in, and what is your connection to the UK (for example, are you a Crown servant, or do you have any other ties to the UK)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not say exactly which country, but I live abroad. I don't work for the UK government or anything like that - no special ties to the UK really. Why do you ask? Is there a way I can still claim even though I'm not living there?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. I ask because the rules for Child Benefit generally require you to live in the UK to qualify. There are some exceptions - for example, if you live in certain countries or if you're a Crown servant - but these are specific circumstances.

Since you've mentioned that you live abroad and don't have special ties to the UK (such as being a Crown servant), let me ask one more important question:

**Does Alex live with you abroad, or does he live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with me abroad. We're together here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Based on what you've told me, I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me carefully consider the rules:

- You live abroad (outside the UK)
- Alex, your 7-year-old son, lives with you abroad
- You are not a Crown servant or working for the UK government
- You don't have other special ties to the UK

According to the Child Benefit rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 **and you live in the UK**. There are exceptions for people who go to live in certain countries or who are Crown servants, but you've indicated that neither of these exceptions apply to your situation.

Since you and Alex both live abroad and you don't fall into one of the specific exception categories, you would not be eligible for UK Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex. The main reason is that UK Child Benefit requires you to live in the UK, and since both you and Alex live abroad and you don't fall into the special exception categories (such as being a Crown servant or living in specific qualifying countries), you do not meet the eligibility criteria.

If your circumstances change in the future - for example, if you move back to the UK - you would then be able to apply for Child Benefit at that time.
